review.verdict: The human closing the door is rendered directly on top of the robot, and the sign's CLOSED text overlaps the robot's face, turning a simple three-beat joke into an illegible overlapping blob — this fails on polish and clarity alone.
revisionNotes: The human 'closer' at x=0.39 overlaps almost exactly with the robot at left-third; move the human to sit right in the nearest doorway opening (around x=0.50) so it reads as emerging from the door, not standing inside the robot.

The CLOSED label attached to the human's sign sits on top of the robot's face and the robot's own CLOSED-reading area, making both unreadable; offset the flip-sign label further right/up so it clears the robot's head entirely.

Scale the doors component up (currently reads as three short stubby rectangles) — brief calls for a row of doorways at varying heights that read as entrances; try scale 1.2-1.3 and raise them so the tops don't crowd the CLOSED labels above them.
The shopping bag is drawn disconnected and floating to the robot's far left instead of swinging from its hand; reduce the offset so it reads as attached/carried.
Increase spacing between the 'closedb' and 'closedc' labels and their doors so no sign overlaps a neighboring shape.
Once the overlap is fixed, confirm the robot's worried expression and antenna cursor-badge are visible — right now the badge is lost behind the overlapping human and sign.

review.verdict: The cast and concept work (robot shopper vs. human closing a door), but the nearest doorway, the human, and the robot are smashed into one illegible overlapping cluster with a stray cursor badge and a mis-placed CLOSED label — this reads as a rendering bug, not a staged scene, and drags the average below the bar.
revisionNotes: The nearest doorway is almost entirely hidden behind the overlapping robot and human figures — pull the robot (left-third) and the 'closer' human apart with a clearer gap so door #1's frame is visible as its own doorway, not a collision of shapes.

Render 'closer' as just an arm/hand poking out of the doorway per the brief, or shrink and re-anchor the full human body so it sits inside door #1's silhouette instead of spilling into the street next to the robot.

The rotated 'flipsign' CLOSED label overlaps the robot's antenna and the cursor-arrow badge — move it clear of the robot's head, or reduce its rotate/offset so the three overlapping elements don't read as a rendering glitch.
Scale the cursor-arrow badge down and anchor it visibly on the robot (e.g. chest or shoulder) instead of floating disconnected in the sky above the cluster.

Left-center of the frame is overcrowded (robot + bag + human + sign + badge) while the right two-thirds only holds two door shapes — widen the spacing so the composition reads as a row of three doors with even visual weight.

review.verdict: The cast and metaphor are clean and kind (robot agent, human closer), but overlapping CLOSED tags, a confusing blank mid-flip sign, elements clipped at the safe-area edges, a half-empty top, and a palette/composition that closely echoes a recent doors-themed slopper pull the average below the bar.
revisionNotes: Separate the two overlapping CLOSED tags: 'flipsign' (attached to closer) and 'closedb' (on door2) currently cross each other — move flipsign's offset left/down or shrink its rotate so there's a visible gap.
The blank sign the human holds (holds:'sign') reads as empty; attach the 'CLOSED' text directly onto that placard instead of a separate floating rotated label, so the mid-flip beat is legible.
Pull 'bag' fully inside the safe margin (offset it further right or scale the robot group) — it's currently clipped at the left edge per the lint warning.
Raise door1's bottom edge or reduce its height slightly so it stays inside the safe area (currently extends to y=1047, flagged by lint).

The top ~50% of the frame is flat empty cream with no secondary element — raise the horizon or add one small prop (cloud, awning) to use the square more intentionally instead of pushing everything into the bottom band.

This door-row/gatekeeping composition (navy-cream duotone, vertical door rectangles, robot vs. human) closely echoes the recent 'RISK/AI doors' slopper — vary the door shape (arches, windows) or palette to read as fresh.
